_comment: Curated A11 reference material: overview, rail circuits, the 2800-series
diagnostic fault codes, component notes, and the caveats where two sources
disagree. Hand-written from §2-100 … §2-117, §5-2 and §5-13 … §5-16 of the
1996 Series II service manual, and from Figure 7-11's six schematic sheets.
Everything here was checked against the manual's own text layer, which is
exact. Where the study document in ../MD/A11_DAC.md and the manual differ,
the manual is followed and the difference is recorded as a caveat.

overview.summary: The basic building block of the calibrator: every other assembly makes its ac and dc voltages and currents out of A11's precision dc voltage, and A11's own adc is what characterises the whole instrument during calibration. It is a pulse-width-modulated DAC rather than a resistor-ladder one. Two square waves of fixed amplitude and software-controlled duty cycle -- a coarse channel switched between the 13 V reference and 0 V, and a fine channel switched between about 0.78 mV and 0 V -- are averaged by a five-pole filter on the plug-in A11A1 SIP whose dominant pole sits near 10 Hz, which is 120 dB of rejection at the 190 Hz switching rate. What comes out is a dc voltage of 0 to 22 V of either polarity with 0.309 mV of coarse resolution and 18.5 nV of fine. Accuracy comes from two heated hybrids: HR5, a 13 V reference of two cascaded temperature-compensated ref amps held at 62 °C, and HR6, a precision op amp and its ratio-matched network held at 50 °C. Around them sit the duty-cycle control (82C54 timer U6, optocouplers U12 and U13, flip-flop U14 and a watchdog that pins the filter input at REFCOM if the 8 MHz clock stops), the output stage and its 60 mA current limit, three correction circuits -- series linearity, shunt linearity and negative offset -- the latching output relays, and the calibration hardware: a 22-bit recirculating-remainder adc (U25) with a gain-of-11 null amplifier in front of it. Because that adc reads the diagnostic line for every other analog board, an A11 fault presents as faults everywhere; confirm A11 before chasing anything it measures.
overview.connectors: P401 and P402, DIN 41612 type C, 64-pin right angle, into J401 and J402 on the Analog Motherboard.
overview.note: A11 runs on more separate rails than any other analog board -- +30 FR1, FR1 COM, +5 FR1, -18 FR1, +5 FR1R, +30 FR2, FR2 COM, -5 FR2 on P401, and ±17 S, S COM, ±44 S, ±5 LH, LH COM, +5 RLH and RLH COM on P402 -- each entering through a 6-turn choke with 0.22 µF bypasses. A rail fault presents as a DAC fault. It also carries three separate commons on purpose: SCOM (TP1), REFCOM (TP3) and ADCCOM (TP12) are isolated so reference currents do not return through the adc, and substituting one for another gives a plausible but wrong reading.

REF.rails: REF13, REF6, 3V, CH1 SERIES A/B, CH1 SHUNT, CH1/CH2 FILTER INPUT
REF.note: The reference and the two duty-cycle channels, which together are the DAC's accuracy. HR5 carries the 13 V reference -- two cascaded 6.5 V temperature-compensated transistor/zener ref amps, biased by a thin-film network so their temperature coefficients cancel -- on a substrate heated to 62 °C by Q1 and Q2 on the main board, with RT2 inside the hybrid stealing base current at about 67 °C to stop a thermal runaway. The coarse channel switches that 13 V through series FETs Q4/Q5 and shunt FET Q6; the fine channel switches a 3 V rail, buffered by U1B and U11, through Q30 and Q32 and then divides it by about 3800 inside HR5. Two correction circuits exist purely because those FETs have 3 to 5 Ω of on-resistance: U38 with Z2 supplies the series switch's filter current, U2B with Q22 and three 80 kΩ resistors in HR6 supplies the shunt switch's.

OUT.rails: DAC OUT HI/LO, DAC SENSE HI/LO, DAC SENSE CAL, DAC/OSC OUT HI/LO, RANGE SELECT
OUT.note: The output stage and the relays that route it. HR6's precision op amp sits inside a feedback loop with output buffer U5, so the dc accuracy is the hybrid's and only the current drive is U5's. RANGE SELECT, crossing the isolation barrier through opto U37, switches Q20/Q21/Q15 and HR6's 40 kΩ feedback pair between unity gain for the 11 V range and a gain of two for the 22 V range. The short-circuit limit is about 60 mA: R23 senses U5's supply current, Q10 turns on at about 50 mA and pulls U5's supply down, Q8 saturates and turns Q11 on to short the input to FR1 COM, and R22 with C41 releases Q11 slowly afterwards so the output does not overshoot. K1 and K2 set the polarity and K1 also generates DAC HI DIAG and DAC LO DIAG; K3 and K4 send the output to the oscillator instead of to everything else during ac operation; K8 in the set position senses the DAC right at the assembly.

ADC.rails: ADC COM, ADC INPUT, ADCAMP OUT/SENSE, REFCAL, RCL, SDL, DAC HI/LO DIAG, ±6.4 V reference, adc +7.5 V and -8.2 V
ADC.note: The calibration hardware, and the reason a fault here shows up as a fault on every other analog board: this adc reads the system diagnostic line (SDL) that A9, A10, A14, A15 and A16 all report through. The adc amplifier is a null detector of gain 11 with high-impedance inputs, its noninverting side switched between ADC COM, RCL and DAC SENSE CAL by K6 and K7 and its inverting side between DAC SENSE CAL and REFCAL by K5; VR19 and VR20 hold its output inside ±4 V and VR17/VR18/VR21/VR22 clamp the inputs. U23 chooses what the adc chip sees -- SDL, DAC HI DIAG divided by R79 and R84, the summed heater voltages divided by R80/R81/R83, or the adc amplifier's own output -- through an R74/C84 filter and buffer U24 that strip 60 Hz and 190 Hz. U25 is a 22-bit Fluke recirculating-remainder converter with about 20 µV of rms noise, cut by a factor of five by averaging.

SUP.rails: +30 FR1, FR1 COM, +5 FR1, -18 FR1, +5 FR1R, +30 FR2, FR2 COM, -5 FR2, ±17 S, S COM, ±44 S, ±5 LH, LH COM, +5 RLH, RLH COM
SUP.note: Nine incoming rails, from the Regulator/Guard Crossing assembly (A17) and the Digital Power Supply (A19), each through a 6-turn choke with 0.22 µF bypasses. The FR1 and FR2 pairs are the floating supplies the duty-cycle side runs on, which is why the optocouplers and transformer T1 exist at all. CR6 and CR8 clamp the ±44 S pair at the connector, and VR1 drops -44 S to -25 S. A11 makes no supply that Chapter 2 tabulates, so there is no Table 2-x to check these against -- the published values are A17's and A19's.

faultCodes.title: A11: 8255 Control Word
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics software reads back the control word of the 82C55 programmable peripheral interface (U31) on the DAC assembly.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates the DAC assembly (A11) is probably at fault. This is a bus-level test and does not depend on any analog circuit, so it fires before anything else can. Suspect U31 and the guarded digital bus into it -- R103-R106 and the P402 data lines -- before looking further.

faultCodes.title: A11: 8255 Port a Wires
faultCodes.measure: Data is written to and read back from port A of U31.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. Port A is the read-only register that carries the adc's readings back to the guarded bus, so this failing means no adc result can reach the software even if the adc is healthy.

faultCodes.title: A11: 8255 Port B Data Bus
faultCodes.measure: Port B of U31 is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. PB0-PB4 drive relays K1-K4 and K6-K8 through drivers U33 and U34, and PB0 is also DAC OUT SEL; a port B fault therefore means the output routing cannot be trusted either.

faultCodes.title: A11: 8254 Status Words
faultCodes.measure: The status of the 82C54 programmable interval timer (U6) is read.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. U6 is the counter that turns each channel count into a duty cycle, so this failing means the DAC has no defined output. Confirm the 8 MHz clock at U6 pin 10 (§5-14 step 1) before replacing U6 -- the chip cannot report sensible status without it.

faultCodes.title: A11: DAC Heaters Not Regulated
faultCodes.measure: With the instrument dormant, the REF HEATER and DCAMP HEATER voltages to the two hybrids are read through U23 by the adc.
faultCodes.hi: U23 pin 7 (via R80, R81 and R83)
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault, but read 2805 first: a cold instrument fails this legitimately. If it has been powered for more than ten minutes, suspect the heater drivers on sheet 1 -- Q1 and Q2 for HR5's 27 Ω element at 62 °C, Q3 for HR6's 42 Ω element at 50 °C -- and check that both moulded hybrid covers (MP1 and MP31) are fitted, because running the board uncovered changes the thermal load enough to fail a good hybrid.

faultCodes.title: 5700 Not Warmed Up
faultCodes.measure: When any heated hybrid in the instrument is found out of regulation, the time since the last reset is checked.
faultCodes.expected: At least ten minutes since reset
faultCodes.verdict: Not an A11-specific code -- it fires for any oven in the instrument -- but it is the companion to 2804 and it is the manual's own definition of warmed up. Wait ten minutes before believing any reference or hybrid measurement on this board.

faultCodes.title: A11: ADC Amp Output Noise
faultCodes.measure: With the instrument dormant, both inputs of the adc amplifier are connected to common and the adc takes ten readings.
faultCodes.expected: Spread between highest and lowest reading no greater than 500 µV
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. This is a noise test with the inputs shorted, so nothing outside the amplifier can cause it: suspect U19, the Z8 network, the ±6.4 V reference chain around VR29, and the adc chip's own supplies at U25 pins 16 and 17. Contamination is a real cause here -- §4-14's warning about skin oil on an analog assembly is aimed at exactly this measurement.

faultCodes.title: A11: ADC Amp Output Offset
faultCodes.measure: With the instrument dormant, both inputs of the adc amplifier are connected to common and the adc takes ten readings.
faultCodes.expected: Average of the ten readings no greater than 3 mV
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. Where 2806 catches noise, this catches a standing offset. Check the buffered ADC COM at U26 pin 7 (§5-15 step 6, 0 V ±600 mV) and the U20B/U26A pair that cancels U19A's current in ADC COM before condemning U19.

faultCodes.title: A11: ADC Amp Gain Error
faultCodes.measure: The DAC is set to 0.1 V on the 11 V range and connected to the adc amplifier's +input with the -input on common. The amplifier's nominal gain of 11 should give 1.1 V out.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. §5-15 step 13 is the bench version of this code: read TP9 against TP10, then TP11 against TP12, and confirm the ratio of 11 within ±15 mV. The gain is set by the Z8 network, so a failure is Z8 or U19 rather than anything programmable.

faultCodes.title: A11: DAC Monitoring Fault
faultCodes.measure: The DAC is set to 1.0 V, routed to the adc through DAC HI DIAG and divided down; the adc reads it. The DAC is then set to 10 V and read again. The divider gain is computed as (10 V - 1 V) / (adc10 - adc1).
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The divider is R79 (100 kΩ 1 %) and R84 (4.7 kΩ), and a gain of 22.13 is the reciprocal of their 4.5 % ratio -- which is also why §5-15 step 1 expects 0.45 V here with the DAC at 10 V. The fault code text names R70 instead of R79; see the caveat. Because this is a ratio taken from two readings, a divider that has drifted fails it while an adc offset does not.

faultCodes.title: A11: +11V DC Range Fault
faultCodes.measure: In the +11 V dc range the DAC is set to 0 V, 1 V and 10 V in turn and its output measured at each setting through DAC HI DIAG by the adc.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The band is far too wide to be a calibration check -- it is looking for a broken output path. Take it with 2811: failing one polarity only points at the polarity relays K1 and K2 and their drivers, while failing both points at the output stage, the filter SIP or the reference.

faultCodes.title: A11: -11V DC Range Fault
faultCodes.measure: In the -11 V dc range the DAC is set to 0 V, -1 V and -10 V in turn and measured at each setting through DAC HI DIAG.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. Negative output is K1 and K2 in the set position, so this failing alone -- with 2810 passing -- is a relay, a driver output on U33/U34, or the port B line that commands them.

faultCodes.title: A11: +22V DC Range Fault
faultCodes.measure: In the +22 V dc range the DAC is set to 0 V, 2 V and 21.9 V in turn and measured at each setting through DAC HI DIAG.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The 22 V range differs from the 11 V range only in RANGE SELECT: Q20 off, Q21 on to switch in HR6's 40 kΩ feedback pair, and Q15 on so the hybrid's output stays near its inputs and the bootstrap keeps working. If 2810 passes and this fails, check RANGE SELECT at U37 pin 7 (§5-13 step 13) before anything else.

faultCodes.title: A11: -22V DC Range Fault
faultCodes.measure: In the -22 V dc range the DAC is set to 0 V, -2 V and -21.9 V in turn and measured at each setting through DAC HI DIAG.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The intersection of 2811 and 2812: negative polarity through K1/K2 and the gain-of-two configuration together. Failing this alone, with 2811 and 2812 both passing, is unusual and worth re-running before acting on.

faultCodes.title: A11: 6.5V Buffered Reference Fault
faultCodes.measure: BRF6 and BSRF6 from the Buffered Reference SIP are connected to the adc amplifier's -input and the DAC output (DAC SENSE CAL) to its +input; the DAC is adjusted until the amplifier nulls.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault, and the bench check is §5-16 step 1: TP1 on the A11A2 SIP should read 6.5 to 7.0 V against TP1 on the main board. Compare with 2815 -- if the raw 6.5 V reference passes and the buffered one fails, the SIP is the fault and the hybrid is not.

faultCodes.title: A11: 6.5V Reference Fault
faultCodes.measure: The raw 6.5 V reference REF6 is connected to the adc amplifier's -input and DAC SENSE CAL to its +input; the DAC is adjusted until the amplifier nulls.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. REF6 is brought out on pin 14 of HR5, so this is the hybrid itself rather than the buffering. Check the 13 V at TP2 first: both references come from the same pair of cascaded ref amps, and 2817 failing alongside this points squarely at HR5.

faultCodes.title: A11: 13V Buffered Reference Fault
faultCodes.measure: BRF13 and BSRF13 from the Buffered Reference SIP are connected to the adc amplifier's -input and DAC SENSE CAL to its +input; the DAC is adjusted until the amplifier nulls.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. Bench equivalent is §5-16 step 2: TP2 on the A11A2 SIP should read 13 to 14 V against TP1 on the main board. As with 2814, compare against the unbuffered code -- 2817 -- to separate the SIP from the hybrid.

faultCodes.title: A11: 13V Reference Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 13 V reference REF13 is connected to the adc amplifier's -input and DAC SENSE CAL to its +input; the DAC is adjusted until the amplifier nulls.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. This is the reference the whole DAC is a fraction of, and TP2 is where to measure it by hand -- §5-13 step 2, +13 to +14 V and very stable. Before condemning HR5, check the supplies feeding it and give the oven its ten minutes.

faultCodes.title: Assembly A11 Missing
faultCodes.measure: At power up the instrument checks which assemblies are not installed and finds the DAC assembly not responding.
faultCodes.expected: A response on the guarded digital bus
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. Before anything else, check the board is actually seated -- this code also fires for a card partly out of J401/J402, or left on the extender with the extender not home. If it is seated, it is U31 or the bus into it, the same suspects as 2800.

faultCodes.title: A11: 8255 Was Reset
faultCodes.measure: The control word of U31 is read and found to be the reset default rather than what was written.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. Unlike 2800 this says the port was configured and then lost it, which points at the RESET line and its pull-up R104 or at a supply glitch on +5 LH rather than at the chip.

faultCodes.title: A11: Fine Adjust Channel Fault
faultCodes.measure: The second channel is set to a count giving 0 V at the DAC output and the output is read by the adc; the count is then increased and the resulting increase in DAC output verified.
faultCodes.expected: The output to move with the count
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault, and it is specifically the fine channel -- worth 18.5 nV a count, so it can fail entirely while every range code passes. The bench path is TP7 (§5-13 step 5): the manual's own test is to vary the second least significant digit of the output with the edit knob and watch the duty cycle at TP7 change.

faultCodes.title: A8/A11: +11/22V DC Zero Estimate Fault
faultCodes.measure: In the +11 V or +22 V range the DAC output (DAC SENSE CAL) goes to the adc amplifier's +input and RCOM to its -input; the DAC is adjusted to null.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault -- but note the code is shared with the Switch Matrix (A8), because RCOM comes from there. A non-convergence is different from an out-of-tolerance reading: it means the loop could not find a null at all, so suspect a stuck relay or an open in the sense path before suspecting an accuracy problem.

faultCodes.title: A8/A11: -11/22V DC Zero Estimate Fault
faultCodes.measure: In the -11 V or -22 V range the DAC output goes to the adc amplifier's +input and RCOM to its -input; the DAC is adjusted to null.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault, with the same A8 caveat as 2821. Failing only the negative version again points at K1 and K2.

faultCodes.title: A11: Couldn't Estimate +11V Or 22V Gain
faultCodes.measure: One of the DAC's references goes to the adc amplifier's -input and DAC SENSE CAL to its +input; the DAC is adjusted to null and the gain estimated from the result.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The reference selection FETs are on the A11A2 SIP and are commanded by the level-shifted control lines out of U35 and U36, so a failure to converge can be a missing select line rather than a bad reference -- which the reference codes 2814 to 2817 would not distinguish.

faultCodes.title: A11: Couldn't Estimate 6.5 MHz Or 13 MHz Ref
faultCodes.measure: One of the DAC's references goes to the adc amplifier's -input and DAC SENSE CAL to its +input; the DAC is adjusted to null and the reference estimated.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The title is a misprint in the manual: there is no 6.5 MHz or 13 MHz anything on this board -- these are the 6.5 V and 13 V references, as the body text says. Same suspects as 2823.

faultCodes.title: A11: Couldn't Est 6.5V Or 13V Buf Ref
faultCodes.measure: One of the buffered references goes to the adc amplifier's -input and DAC SENSE CAL to its +input; the DAC is adjusted to null and the buffered reference estimated.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A11 is probably at fault. The buffered-reference version of 2824: the buffers are on the A11A2 SIP, so measure its TP1 and TP2 by hand (§5-16) before replacing anything on the main board.

faultCodes.title: A11: A/D Overload Fault
faultCodes.measure: A positive and then a negative overload is applied to the adc input and the resulting adc output compared against the expected overload reading.
faultCodes.expected: The published overload readings for both polarities
faultCodes.verdict: A failure on either polarity indicates A11 is at fault -- the manual states this one flatly rather than saying 'probably'. It tests the adc chip's own behaviour past full scale, so it exercises U25, its ±6.4 V reference and the Z10 network rather than anything in front of them.

componentNotes.HR5: The Reference Hybrid: the 13 V reference the entire calibrator's accuracy rests on, stock 893334, and not field-repairable. A ceramic substrate carrying two cascaded 6.5 V temperature-compensated transistor/zener ref amps (U6 and U7 inside the hybrid, which are not this board's U6 and U7) bonded to a thin-film resistor network, held at 62 °C by a heater screened on the back of the substrate. REF13 HI is pin 9, REF13 SENSE pin 12, REF6 pin 14. It also carries the 100 kΩ/30 kΩ divider that makes the 3 V source, the ÷3800 divider for the second channel, the 19.996 kΩ resistor the series linearity circuit works through, and the divider that makes the -127 mV negative offset. The Rev 9 list gives it stock 761338 instead -- see the caveat.
componentNotes.HR6: The DC Amplifier Hybrid, stock 761411: a low-noise low-offset precision op amp with a bootstrapped supply on a heated ceramic substrate, bonded to a ratio-matched resistor network, held at 50 °C. Pin 18 is its output and is where §5-13 step 10 measures. Its 40 kΩ pair sets the 22 V range's gain of two, its 80 kΩ trio sets the shunt linearity amplifier's gain, its 20 kΩ pair makes the negative offset inverter, and four more of its resistors form the sense current cancellation circuit. Precise ratio matching inside the hybrid is what makes the 22 V range accurate.
componentNotes.A1: The DAC Filter SIP (A11A1), stock 761395: a plug-in board carrying the five-pole active filter that averages the two duty-cycle waveforms into dc. Its dominant pole is near 10 Hz, giving 120 dB of rejection at the 190 Hz switching rate. It also makes the 15 V rail that R111 uses to pull up RANGE SELECT. Its own TP1 is the filter output, checked by §5-13 step 9. Table 6-12 lists it as 'A1'; the theory calls it A11A1 and schematic sheet 1 labels it A93, drawing 5700A-4043.
componentNotes.A2: The DAC Buffered Reference SIP (A11A2), stock 764639: buffers the 6.5 V and 13 V references into BRF6/BSRF6 and BRF13/BSRF13 for the rest of the calibrator, and switches the references or their buffered versions onto the REFCAL line for the adc during calibration. §5-16 troubleshoots it and its two test points are TP1 (6.5 to 7.0 V) and TP2 (13 to 14 V), both referenced to TP1 on the main board. Every designator §5-16 names -- U1A, U2A, Q3, Q4, U1B, U2B, Q10, Q11 -- is on this SIP, not on A11.
componentNotes.U5: Output buffer, an OPA548 power op amp inside HR6's feedback loop: it provides the DAC's current drive while the hybrid provides the accuracy. Short-circuit limited to about 60 mA by R23, Q10, Q8 and Q11. Its parts-list description is truncated in this dataset because the printed row wraps mid-field; the full text is 'IC,OP AMP,OPA548,+-4 TO +-30V,10MV OFFSET,1MHZ,HI V-I,TO-220-7'.
componentNotes.U6: 82C54 programmable interval timer, the heart of the duty-cycle control. It receives a 16-bit count per channel over the guarded bus and turns each into a TTL square wave whose duty cycle is proportional to the count -- OUT1 (pin 16) is the coarse first channel, OUT2 (pin 20) the fine second. Duty-cycle resolution is 0.0024 %.
componentNotes.U7: High-speed comparator that squares the low-level 400 mV p-p differential clock (CLK, CLK*) from the Regulator/Guard Crossing assembly (A17) into the TTL 8 MHz that U6 and the adc chip U25 run on.
componentNotes.U10: The second clock comparator: the same low-level CLK/CLK* pair, isolated by transformer T1 onto the floating side, squared up here to clock the U14 flip-flop. §5-14 step 5 measures it at pin 4 with the common on TP3, not TP1.
componentNotes.U11: Buffers the 3 V that HR5's 100 kΩ/30 kΩ divider makes from the 13 V reference, giving the second channel its switched amplitude. §5-14 step 12 measures pin 3 for a nominal 3 V.
componentNotes.U12: Optocoupler carrying the second channel across the isolation barrier to become CH2 FLOATING, which drives Q30 and Q32.
componentNotes.U13: 20 MHz optocoupler carrying the first channel across to become CH1 FLOATING. Faster than U12 because the coarse channel's edges matter far more.
componentNotes.U14: Dual D flip-flop. One half re-clocks CH1 FLOATING against the 8 MHz to give the coarse channel accurate edges: Q1 (pin 5) is CH1 SERIES A driving Q7, Q1* (pin 6) becomes CH1 SHUNT via Q35 and CH1 SERIES B via Q33/Q34. The other half divides the clock to 4 MHz for the watchdog. Its preset is what the watchdog pulls to force the filter input to REFCOM.
componentNotes.U15: Dual monostable used as the watchdog timer. With C63 and R48 it is retriggered by the 4 MHz clock; if that clock stops, C63 charges, Q1 goes low and presets U14 so the shunt switch is on and the series switch off. The DAC then sits at zero instead of at an arbitrary voltage.
componentNotes.U19: The adc amplifier: a dual precision matched op amp with a gain of 11, used as a null detector between DAC SENSE CAL, RCL, REFCAL and ADC COM. Its gain is set by the Z8 network. Fault codes 2806, 2807 and 2808 are its noise, offset and gain tests.
componentNotes.U20: Precision dual op amp; U20A cancels the current U19A generates in ADC COM, and U20B works with U26A on the -6.4 V reference. A fault here shows as an adc offset (2807) rather than as a dead circuit.
componentNotes.U22: Buffers DAC LO DIAG so that the two heater diagnostic lines, which are referenced to FR1 COM rather than to the adc's common, have a proper current return. §5-15 step 3 checks its pin 6 for 0 V ±11 mV against TP1.
componentNotes.U23: Quad DMOS analog switch, the adc input selector: SDL for other assemblies' diagnostics, DAC HI DIAG divided by R79 and R84, the summed heater lines divided by R80/R81/R83, or the adc amplifier's own output. Its control lines come from U35, U36 and port C of U31.
componentNotes.U24: Buffer after the R74/C84 filter that strips 60 Hz and 190 Hz off the adc input before it reaches U25 pin 22. §5-15 step 2 names it, not U25, as the suspect when the level is right at U23 pin 7 and wrong at the chip.
componentNotes.U25: The adc chip: a 22-bit converter using Fluke's patented recirculating-remainder technique, with about 20 µV of rms noise between readings, reduced fivefold by averaging. Its own supplies are +7.5 V at pin 16 (VR27, R77) and -8.2 V at pin 17 (VR28, R94), both referenced to SCOM. It sits in the 40-pin socket X1.
componentNotes.U26: Dual low-noise op amp; U26A works with U20B on the -6.4 V reference and the buffered ADC COM checked by §5-15 step 6.
componentNotes.U27: Dual JFET-input op amp; U27B inverts the -6.4 V reference to make the +6.4 V checked at pin 1 by §5-15 step 8.
componentNotes.U29: JFET-input op amp in the adc's sample-and-hold bootstrap supply, with Q56, Q57 and VR31-VR34. Its pin 7 and pin 4 carry the ±bootstrap rails, which follow the held voltage and so have deliberately wide published bands.
componentNotes.U31: 82C55 programmable peripheral interface, the board's entire digital interface. Port A returns adc readings to the guarded bus; PB0-PB4 drive relays K1-K4 and K6-K8 through U33 and U34 and PB0 is also DAC OUT SEL; PB5-PB7 are decoded by U32; port C carries RANGE SELECT, ADC TRIGGER, the clock and first-channel shutdown used in the resistance function, and the U23 and adc-amplifier select lines. Fault codes 2800-2802, 2818 and 2819 all test it.
componentNotes.U32: 3-to-8 line decoder turning PB5-PB7 into the six adc-amplifier input select lines, one of which is K5SEL.
componentNotes.U33: 8-channel high-voltage driver with latch, controlling latching relays K7 and K8 and feeding U34.
componentNotes.U34: 8-channel high-voltage driver with latch, controlling latching relays K1-K6.
componentNotes.U35: Quad comparator level-shifting four of the decoded select lines -- BSRF6 SEL, BSRF13 SEL, REF6 SEL and REF13 SEL -- for the FETs on the Buffered Reference SIP.
componentNotes.U36: Quad comparator level-shifting ADC COM SEL, DAC DIAG SEL, HEATER SEL and ADCAMP OUT SEL for the FETs in U23 and on the SIP.
componentNotes.U37: Optocoupler carrying RANGE SELECT across to the analog side, pulled up by R111 to the 15 V made on the DAC Filter SIP. §5-13 step 13 reads its pin 7: -16 to -19 V in the 11 V range, +4 to +11 V in the 22 V range.
componentNotes.U38: The series linearity control amplifier. With Z2 and a 19.996 kΩ resistor in HR5 it supplies the filter current that would otherwise flow through series switch Q5, whose 3 to 5 Ω of on-resistance would otherwise be a linearity error. §5-13 step 6 reads its pin 6 for +23.0 to +26.4 V.
componentNotes.Z2: The 5700 low-voltage divider network, a poly SIP, working with U38 in the series linearity control circuit.
componentNotes.Z8: The 5700 low-voltage instrumentation amplifier network, hermetic, that sets the adc amplifier's gain of 11. Fault code 2808 is really a test of this part.
componentNotes.Z10: The 5700 A-to-D converter network, hermetic: the precision ladder the recirculating-remainder adc works against. Its printed values -- 50K, 100K, 200K, 400K, 800K, 1.6M against 15.238K, 159.97K and 10.667K -- are the converter's own scaling.
componentNotes.T1: Pulse transformer isolating the low-level 8 MHz CLK/CLK* pair onto the floating reference side, where U10 squares it up for the U14 flip-flop. The only magnetic part on the board apart from the supply chokes.
componentNotes.X1: 40-pin dual-wipe IC socket. It has no silkscreen designator of its own -- it sits under U25, the adc chip.
componentNotes.K1: Latching relay, 4 form C. With K2 it sets the DAC output polarity: reset is positive, set is negative. K1 also generates DAC LO DIAG and DAC HI DIAG for the self-diagnostics.
componentNotes.K2: Latching relay, 4 form C, the other half of the polarity pair.
componentNotes.K3: Latching relay, 2 form C. With K4 it routes the DAC output: reset makes it available to every assembly except the oscillator, set connects it to the DAC/OSC lines during ac operation.
componentNotes.K4: Latching relay, 4 form C, the other half of the output routing pair.
componentNotes.K5: Latching relay, 2 form C, selecting the adc amplifier's inverting input between DAC SENSE CAL and REFCAL. §5-15 step 11 measures its output at TP10.
componentNotes.K6: Latching relay, 2 form C, part of the noninverting input selection between ADC COM, RCL and DAC SENSE CAL. Present on the drawing and in the sheet 1 legend but omitted from Table 6-12 -- see the caveat.
componentNotes.K7: Latching relay, 2 form C, the other half of the noninverting input selection. Omitted from Table 6-12 in the same way as K6. §5-15 step 12 names both when TP9 reads wrong.
componentNotes.K8: Latching relay, 2 form C. In the set position it lets the DAC be sensed right at the assembly output.
componentNotes.Q1: TIP120 driving the HR5 reference hybrid's 27 Ω heater element at 62 °C. Not to be confused with 'the Q1 output of U14' in §5-14 step 8, which is a flip-flop pin.
componentNotes.Q2: TIP32 in the HR5 heater control loop; the thermistor inside the hybrid works against its base.
componentNotes.Q3: TIP32 providing power to the HR6 dc amplifier hybrid's 42 Ω heater element at 50 °C.
componentNotes.Q9: The fourth TO-220 on the left edge, in the heater control circuitry with Q1, Q2 and Q3. Sheet 1's package legend groups it with Q8, Q10 and Q19.
componentNotes.VR29: The adc's -6.4 V reference: the only temperature-compensated zener on the board, 6.4 V ±2 % at 2 ppm/°C, stock 419036. It sets the adc's scale, so a drift here is a calibration error across every range the instrument has rather than a hard failure.
componentNotes.R79: 100 kΩ 1 %, the top of the DAC HI DIAG divider. With R84 (4.7 kΩ) it divides the DAC output by about 22.13 for the self-diagnostics -- 0.45 V from a 10 V output, which is what §5-15 step 1 expects.
componentNotes.R84: 4.7 kΩ, the bottom of the DAC HI DIAG divider with R79.
componentNotes.R111: 33 kΩ pull-up for RANGE SELECT, returned to the 15 V generated on the DAC Filter SIP rather than to a rail on this board.
componentNotes.R23: 6.8 Ω surface-mount sense resistor in U5's supply lead: the current sense that starts the 60 mA short-circuit limit when about 50 mA develops enough voltage across it to turn Q10 on. The Rev 9 list gives this position as 10 Ω -- see the caveat.
componentNotes.L10: 6-turn choke at the output buffer's output, and the point §5-13 step 11 measures for +10 V. It is a filter, not a component under test; what is being checked through it is U5.
componentNotes.M2: Sheet-metal shield over the DAC-adc amplifier section. Separate from the front and rear shields, and it only needs to come off for §5-15 work.
componentNotes.M3: The rear DAC shield. §5-13 step 1 has it off along with the front shields before the board goes on the extender.
componentNotes.H32: The front DAC shield, removed with MP11 and M3 at §5-13 step 1.
componentNotes.MP1: Moulded cover over the hybrid resistor network. Leaving it off changes the thermal load and can fail fault code 2804 on a good hybrid.
componentNotes.MP31: Moulded cover over the reference hybrid, with the same warning as MP1.
componentNotes.MP4: Static shielding bag, 10 × 14 inch -- packaging, listed only in the Rev 9 parts list.
componentNotes.H2: C-MOS handling form -- paperwork, listed only in the Rev 9 parts list. Nine of A11's parts are marked ESD-sensitive including both hybrids and both SIPs.

caveats.title: One procedure here, four sections in the manual
caveats.text: Chapter 5 prints A11's troubleshooting as §5-13 (16 steps), §5-14 Duty-cycle Control Circuit (13 steps), §5-15 ADC Circuit (14 steps) and §5-16 Buffered Reference SIP Assembly (2 steps), each numbered from 1. The app shows one procedure of 45 steps, so §5-14's steps are 17-29 here, §5-15's are 30-43 and §5-16's are 44-45; §5-13's are unchanged. Each step still says which section it was printed in. This is not the manual's numbering and it is not claimed to be: unlike A14, where §5-19 step 6 refers forward to 'step 10' and so implies a single sequence, A11's sections hand off to each other by name -- §5-13 steps 3, 4 and 5 all say 'skip to Duty Cycle Control Circuit'. The renumbering exists because the viewer walks one procedure per board. Expectations authored against §5-14, §5-15 and §5-16 cite the combined number and give the printed number in their note, so nothing here can attach an expectation to the wrong step.

caveats.title: §5-16 troubleshoots a different assembly
caveats.text: §5-16 is printed inside A11's troubleshooting but every measurement and every suspect in it is on the plug-in DAC Buffered Reference SIP (A11A2). Its U1A, U2A, Q3, Q4, U1B, U2B, Q10, Q11, TP1 and TP2 are the SIP's; A11 has parts of all those names and they are different parts. The section is kept because a technician following §5-13 arrives at it, but its designator links are suppressed and the two measurements are carried as probe points that name the SIP. The same applies to §5-13 step 9, which measures TP1 on the DAC Filter SIP (A11A1) while A11's own TP1 is SCOM.

caveats.title: Table 6-12 omits K6 and K7
caveats.text: The 1996 parts list prints 'K3,K5,K8  RELAY,ARMATURE,2 FORM C,5V,LATCH  769307  3'. The Rev 9 list prints the same part as 'K 3, 5-8' with a quantity of 5, and the drawing, the sheet 1 relay legend ('2FCL BOTTOM VIEW  K3, K5-K8') and the sheet 6 drive circuit all show K6 and K7 as real relays -- §5-15 step 12 tells you to check them by name when TP9 reads wrong. K6 and K7 are carried here from the Rev 9 list and marked as Rev-9-only for that reason. They are not new parts; the 1996 row simply lost two designators and its quantity was not corrected.

caveats.title: Fault code 2809 names R70; the divider is R79
caveats.text: Code 2809 says the 1 V and 10 V readings are 'divided by R70 and R84 on the DAC'. §5-15 step 1 and §2-114 both say R79 and R84, and the schematic bears them out: sheet 5 shows DAC HI DIAG entering through R79 (100 kΩ 1 %) with R84 (4.7 kΩ) below it, a ratio of 4.49 % -- which is why the same step expects 0.45 V from a 10 V output and why 2809's own nominal gain is 22.13. R70 is a 20 kΩ 0.1 % resistor in the adc amplifier and has nothing to do with the divider. Read 2809 as R79.

caveats.title: The two parts lists disagree about the zeners, and about R23
caveats.text: Eleven zener rows fail to join on stock number between the two revisions, and the pattern is consistent: the 1996 list specifies surface-mount SOT-23 parts and the Rev 9 list the leaded 0.4 W 1N9xx equivalents the earlier boards were built with -- VR4 is 876433 (SOT-23) against 810325 (1N967B), VR7/VR16 831230 against 811927, and so on. Those are recorded as 'as built' and either part works. One row is a real value change rather than a package change: R23 is 6.8 Ω in the 1996 list and 10 Ω in the Rev 9 list. R23 is the current sense in the output buffer's supply lead that sets the 60 mA short-circuit limit, so the two revisions limit at different currents. HR5 also changed stock number, 761338 to 893334.

caveats.title: TP8's three checks do not agree on the common
caveats.text: §5-13 step 12 measures TP8 '(common to TP12)'; steps 14 and 16 measure the same point '(common to TP3)'. TP12 is ADCCOM and TP3 is REFCOM MECCA POINT, and §2-115 is explicit that the two are deliberately separate so reference currents do not return through the adc. The DAC output is defined against REFCOM, so TP3 is followed here and step 12's TP12 is recorded rather than acted on. The difference is small enough that a ±0.25 V check will not show it -- which is exactly why it is worth knowing before making a fine measurement.

caveats.title: Three names for each SIP
caveats.text: §2-100 calls them A11A1 and A11A2. Table 6-12 lists them as A1 and A2, which is how they appear in this dataset because that is the designator on the parts row. Schematic sheet 1 labels the same two boards A93 (drawing 5700A-4043) and A94 (drawing 5700A-4044), and the Manual Status Information table on page 6-4 lists them a fourth way, as A93 and A95. They are all the same two parts, stock 761395 and 764639.

caveats.title: Q27 and J21 are on the board but in no parts list
caveats.text: The locator drawing prints Q27 between Q25 and C9 with no component outline around it -- an unstuffed position -- and it appears in neither the 1996 nor the Rev 9 list. J21 is the large rectangular outline between C111 and C110 where the DAC Filter SIP plugs in; it too has no parts-list line, the sheets naming the same connections P21/P22 and J2A/J2B instead. Neither is offered as a part here, and a reader who finds those legends on the board and cannot search for them is not missing anything.

caveats.title: Table 6-12's second 10 kΩ row is printed with a quantity of zero
caveats.text: The 1996 list gives 'R19-21,R29,R31,R41,R48 ... 746610 ... 10' -- seven designators against a quantity of ten -- and then 'R82,R115,R116 ... 746610 ... 0'. The ten covers both rows; the second row's own quantity is left at zero rather than repeated. Nothing is missing, but any count taken from the quantity column of this table will be wrong by three.

caveats.title: The revision comes from the photograph, not the drawing
caveats.text: The board is silkscreened 'DAC ASSY 761122 REV' with the letter left blank and stamped per board. The locator drawing carries the same blank field -- it prints 'DAC REV' at the right-hand edge with nothing after it -- so unlike A18 there is no revision on the artwork. The photographed board reads REV P. The Manual Status Information table gives the assembly's revision level as 104, which is a different numbering again.

caveats.title: The schematic's S and 5 are nearly the same glyph
caveats.text: Figure 7-11's lettering renders a capital S almost identically to a 5, and this board's net names are full of both. '+17S' reads as '+175', 'SCOM' as '5COM', '+5 FR1' as '+S FR1'. The rails are +17 S, -17 S, +44 S, -44 S and their buffered versions +17 SB and -17 SB; the 5 V rails are +5 FR1, +5 FR1R, -5 FR2, ±5 LH and +5 RLH. Worth knowing before reading a net name off a sheet, and worth remembering when reviewing anything a machine read off one.
